newsitem.title: FRANCE: AGF upbeat on earnings after profit jump.
newsitem.headline: AGF upbeat on earnings after profit jump.

text.p: French insurer AGF, privatised last July, reported on Thursday a 48.5 percent jump in half-year profit and was confident about its earnings prospects.
Net attributable profit climbed to 723 million francs from 487 million on premium income up 5.4 percent to 33.8 billion.

AGF said the results reflected a turnaround in its non-life business along with a strong performance by its insurance activities outside France and added it was on track to achieving its aim of a 10 percent return on equity by end 1999.
Return on equity for the half year was 6.3 percent, it said.

Assurances Generales de France (AGF) also said it was on target to attaining its goal of doubling by 1997 the 880 million francs profit it posted in 1994 which was a low point in its earnings cycle. Last year's full-year profit was 1.08 billion.
"We are on track," said finance director Guillaume Hannezo.
AGF added it was way ahead on a two-year asset disposal programme announced at its privatisation, having already sold more 5.76 billion francs worth of property.
The operations would be recorded in its second half accounts and cash generated from the opeations had been reinvested in securities "which should offer a substantially higher yield".
AGF also said it had sold 2.75 billion francs worth of stocks for a capital gain of 883 million francs. It has plans to sell a total five to seven billion francs of equity stakes.

Life insurance kicked in 131 million francs to earnings before exceptional items, down from 344 million for the same period in 1995. Life insurance premiums slipped 19.2 percent but stripping out last year's impact of the successful one-off impact of its Valorea contract, revenues rose by 8.8 percent.
Life insurance capital gains rose to 579 million francs from 1.47 billion. But unrealised capital gains rose to 4.08 billion from 3.44 billion at the end of last year.

Non-life insurance contributed 364 million francs to results, up by nearly 12 percent, reflecting a rise in underwriting profit at AGF IART in France which rose by 19 percent to 1.45 billion. AGF had unrealised capital losses of 399 million at the end of June 1995 compared with unrealised capital gains of 343 million at June 30 1996.

Credit insurance's contribution fell to 159 million from 175 million. That included a 30 million adjustment to goodwill for French export insurance agency Coface booked in its 1995 accounts. Excluding this, the earnings contribution was up by nearly 10 percent despite a bleak economic climate.
Reinsurance contributed 96 million francs, down from 107 million, reflecting deconsolidation of reinsurer Scor.

Business was particularly strong outside France. Its Spanish unit swung back to a profit of 27 million from a loss of 53 million. The Canadian unit had half year earnings of 17 million compared with a loss of five million. The Belgian unit's profits rose to 225 million from 125 million while the Irish unit's profits climbed to 53 million from 22 million.

Banking activties showed a loss of 346 million compared with a loss of 203 million. This reflected a 245 million franc addition to the general banking risks reserve to cover losses on future disposals.

Its troubled real estate finanancing arm Comptoir des Entrepreneurs cut its loss to 32.5 million francs from 67 million. But the loss contributed by Banque du Phenix rose to 51 million from 36 million a year earlier. AGF officials reiterated that they wanted to dispose of Phenix but could not say when.

Property units contributed a loss of 67 million francs compared with a loss of seven million a year earlier, reflecting a rise in provisions. But the losses of the group's holding companies were slashed to 37 million francs from 466 million, reflecting capital gains on sale of investments and reduced debt servicing costs as a result of lower interest rates.
